A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NCGSB/CWG research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–G are readable and can be matched across the layout changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original CWG experiments on LiDAR navigation, cell sequencing and image generation, including measured errors, training times, ablations and qualitative outputs in Section 6 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their quantitative and qualitative outcomes in Section 6 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The NCGSB formulation, ResNet parameterization, training losses, guidance procedure and two-stage training algorithm remain unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic, LiDAR, embryoid-body, sea-temperature, robotic, FFHQ and MNIST-to-EMNIST tasks, including guidance and deblurring. Unpaired image matching is newly mentioned in v4's introduction but was already evaluated in v3.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained: GSBM/DSBM for LiDAR, DM-SB/SBIRR for cell sequencing, and GSBM/DSBM/SB-Flow in the image comparisons (Tables 2–7 and 38).

E3.justification: The cell and sea-temperature held-out-time protocols, FFHQ 60K/10K split, evaluation metrics, model configurations and batch settings are unchanged. Appendix G introduces no new or revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The cell energy-variation ablation (Table 21 and Figure 13), FFHQ energy-profile comparisons (Figure 10), and guidance comparisons (Tables 6 and 17) retain the same analyses and evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten evaluations from training runs with different initial conditions, summarized using means and standard deviations (Appendix G.1). The FFHQ age-uncertainty calculation in Equation (73) and p-value reporting in Table 7 are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative findings are retained. For example, CWG's LiDAR optimality remains 1.40±0.02 (Table 2), and its cell-validation errors remain 1.11±0.06 and 0.33±0.02 (Table 3). Reframing Figures 3–4 preserves their plotted examples.

T1.justification: Formal definitions, Propositions 1–2, equations, Hamiltonian derivations, stability arguments and complexity analysis are retained. Section 5 revises a verbal energy interpretation without changing the mathematical definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about non-conservative bridges, the near-linear CWG solver and guided generation. The added introductory mention of unpaired matching summarizes existing evidence.

C2.justification: Section 5 changes the stated interpretation of the unchanged Jacobi factor Φ=H−F−B from encoding potential energy to encoding kinetic energy. This locally revises the geometric explanation; experimental interpretations and the stated memory limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices F–G retain the same Wasserstein estimator, architecture and hyperparameter tables, hardware, preprocessing instructions and resource pointers. No implementation or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Source-guided flow matching changes from a 2025 preprint citation to its ICLR 2026 publication; other changes add bibliographic links and backreferences without introducing new works.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized wording and grammar edits, expands the explanation of the potential term in Equation (2), updates affiliations and email information, and fixes appendix spacing. Section order and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 3–4 are resized and reframed, Figure 1's caption is revised, and existing displays shift within a more compact main-text layout. Figure 10 moves from page 11 to page 10, and bibliography page backreferences are added. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The fuller explanation of Equation (2), revised energy interpretation in Section 5 and bibliography backreferences modestly improve clarity and navigation. Reflow keeps Proposition 2 together but splits Equation (4) across pages. The net gain is limited, with the same methods, formal analysis and empirical evidence retained.
